text: The word of the LORD came to me:
Son of man, set your face toward the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them.

Say: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD! This is what the Lord GOD says to the mountains and the hills, to the ravines and the valleys: I myself am bringing a sword against you, and I will destroy your high places.

versions.text: Say: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD! This is what the Lord GOD says to the mountains and the hills, to the ravines and the valleys: I am about to bring a sword against you, and I will destroy your high places.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew הִנְנִי אֲנִי is emphatic ("I myself"), stressing that the LORD personally brings the sword. The emphasis is lost in the current rendering.

text: Your altars will be laid waste and your incense stands smashed, and I will throw down your slain before your idols.
I will lay the corpses of the Israelites before their idols, and I will scatter your bones around your altars.

Wherever you live, the cities will lie in ruins and the high places will be desolate, so that your altars are ruined and left guilty, your idols smashed and finished, your incense stands cut down, and everything you have made wiped away.
The slain will fall in your midst, and you will know that I am the LORD.
Yet I will leave a remnant: some of you will escape the sword among the nations, when you are scattered through the lands.

Then your survivors will remember me among the nations where they have been carried captive—how I broke their adulterous heart that turned away from me and their eyes that lusted after their idols. They will loathe themselves to their own faces for the evils they have done, for all their detestable practices.

versions.text: Then your survivors will remember me among the nations where they have been carried captive—how I broke their adulterous heart that turned away from me and their eyes that lusted after their idols. They will loathe themselves for the evils they have done, for all their detestable practices.
versions.explanation: The idiom בִּפְנֵיהֶם ("in/to their faces") intensifies the self-loathing; if the compact form is preferred for oral flow, consider a footnote noting the literal sense "loathe themselves to their own faces."

text: And they will know that I am the LORD; I did not threaten in vain to bring this disaster upon them.
This is what the Lord GOD says: Clap your hands, stamp your foot, and cry out, "Alas!" over all the wicked abominations of the house of Israel, for they will fall by sword, famine, and plague.

versions.text: This is what the Lord GOD says: Clap your hands, stamp your foot, and cry out, "Alas!" over all the vile and detestable practices of the house of Israel, for they will fall by sword, famine, and plague.
versions.explanation: "Vile" and "detestable" are near-synonyms in English, blurring the two Hebrew words תּוֹעֲבוֹת (detestable things) and רָעוֹת (evil). "Evil and detestable" renders the pair more clearly.

versions.text: This is what the Lord GOD says: Clap your hands, stamp your foot, and cry out, "Alas!" over all the evil and detestable practices of the house of Israel, for they will fall by sword, famine, and plague.
versions.explanation: In Hebrew תּוֹעֲבוֹת רָעוֹת is a noun with a qualifying adjective ("evil abominations"), not two coordinated nouns. Rendering it as an adjective plus noun ("wicked abominations") keeps the two Hebrew words distinct — the concern that prompted the earlier revision — while reflecting the grammatical relationship and reading more tightly aloud.

text: The one far away will die of plague, the one near will fall by the sword, and whoever is left and survives will die of famine. So I will spend my fury on them.

Then you will know that I am the LORD, when their slain lie among their idols around their altars—on every high hill, on all the mountaintops, under every green tree and every leafy oak, wherever they offered fragrant incense to all their idols.
I will stretch out my hand against them and make the land a desolate waste, from the wilderness to Diblah, wherever they live. Then they will know that I am the LORD.[fn]

versions.text: I will stretch out my hand against them and make the land a desolate waste, from the wilderness to Diblah, wherever they live. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
versions.explanation: A footnote would help readers: "Diblah" is otherwise unknown; many take it as a scribal variant of Riblah in the far north, so the phrase means "from end to end of the land."
